chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there something fixed regarding the recitation in the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, except for the Friday prayer. You recite in it Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fixed Quranic recitation in daily prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of recitation (qira'ah) in the first two rak'ahs of daily prayers, establishing that while no specific surah is obligatory, the Friday prayer uniquely mandates the recitation of Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential status of Jumu'ah within Shia tradition, where these two surahs are recited in the first and second rak'ahs respectively, reflecting their thematic emphasis on communal leadership and divine signs. The hadith serves as a foundational text for distinguishing between general voluntary recitation and the specific Sunnah obligations of the Friday congregational prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The recitation in the Salāt, is there something fixed therein?’ Heasws said: ‘No, except for the Friday Salāt. You should recite during it, the (Surah) Jumma (Chapter 62) and the (Surah) Munafiqeen (Chapter 63)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is there any temporary recitation in Salah (prayer)? He (the Imam) replied, ‘No, except Friday in which you recite al-Jumu‘ah, and al-Munafiqun, (Chapters 62 and 63).’”
